lesson.title: Joining Text
lesson.driving_question: How can separate pieces of text be joined into one useful value?
lesson.primary_concept_family: Building new strings by concatenating text values
lesson.concept_budget: Join strings with +; number-to-string conversion and formatting syntax are deferred.
misconceptions: The + operator joins strings only when both operands are text.
Concatenation creates a new string value.
A comma in print() is not stored as part of the string.
lesson.progression_note: Completes the core Grade 7 text manipulation strand before random values.

shared_program.code:
first_name = input("First name: ")
last_name = input("Last name: ")
username = first_name.lower() + "." + last_name.lower()
print("Username:", username)

primm.prompt: Recall how lower() returns changed text and how a literal such as a full stop can be stored inside quotes.
Use Asha and Khan. Track each lower-case value and the full stop before writing the final username.
Run with Asha and Khan, then with JO and LI. Check that exactly one full stop separates the two parts.

questions: Why must a separator such as a full stop be added explicitly when two strings are joined?
Why does entering digits for a name still concatenate text instead of performing addition?
For inputs Ava and Li, what username would appear if both lower() calls were removed?

primm.prompt: Use an underscore instead of a full stop. Asha and Khan should produce asha_khan.
Add a department input. Build account_label from lower-case last name, a hyphen and upper-case department. Khan and art should display khan-ART.
Create an event tag from a venue, an activity and a two-letter group. The visible tag must use the structure venue/activity-GROUP with the venue and activity in lower case.
Repair the missing string separator and the misspelled variable name so the username can be joined.
